$$\max(\deg f, \deg g, \deg h) \leq \deg(\operatorname{rad}(fgh)) - 1.$$

$$\max(\deg F, \deg G, \deg(F-G)) \leq \deg(\operatorname{rad}(F)) + \deg(\operatorname{rad}(G)) + \deg(\operatorname{rad}(F-G)) - 1.$$
Since $\operatorname{rad}(F) \mid \operatorname{rad}(A)$ and $\operatorname{rad}(G) \mid \operatorname{rad}(B)$:
$$\max(\deg F, \deg G, \deg(F\!-\!G)) \leq a + b + \deg(F\!-\!G) - 1. \tag{$\star$}$$

**Case 1: $100a \neq 99b$.** The leading terms of $A^{100}$ and $B^{99}$ have different degrees, so no cancellation occurs:
$$\deg C = \max(100a,\, 99b).$$

$$9900k - \deg D \leq 99k + 100k + \deg(F\!-\!G) - 1,$$
$$\deg(F\!-\!G) \geq 9900k - \deg D - 199k + 1.$$
Therefore:
$$\deg C = \deg D + \deg(F\!-\!G) \geq 9900k - 199k + 1 = 9701k + 1 \geq 9702.$$

This is far larger than any value achievable in Case 1.

| $(1, 3)$ | $\max(100, 297) = 297$ |
| $(2, 2)$ | $\max(200, 198) = 200$ |
